generated_plan.title: 6-Month Backend Developer Learning Plan (C#/.NET Core)
generated_plan.goal: Become a job-ready Backend Developer for the global startup market, leveraging C# and .NET Core.
focus_areas: Building robust and secure RESTful APIs
System design fundamentals and scalability concepts

months.theme: C# Deep Dive & ASP.NET Core Fundamentals
months.focus: Solidify C# advanced features, understand ASP.NET Core Web API basics.

topics: C# Advanced Features: Async/Await, LINQ, Generics, Delegates, Events
Object-Oriented Design Principles: SOLID, Design Patterns (Factory, Repository, Singleton - when applicable)
activities: Solve LeetCode Easy/Medium problems focused on C# features.
Refactor existing personal projects applying SOLID principles.
Read 'C# in a Nutshell' (relevant chapters) or equivalent documentation.

topics: .NET Core Fundamentals: CLI, Project Structure, Middleware Pipeline
ASP.NET Core Web API: Controllers, Routing, Action Results, Dependency Injection
Introduction to Swagger/OpenAPI for API documentation
activities: Build a simple CRUD API (e.g., a 'Task Manager' or 'Book List' API) from scratch.
Experiment with different HTTP verbs and request/response types.
Generate and explore Swagger documentation for your API.

months.project_milestone: Basic CRUD API with C# and ASP.NET Core, documented with Swagger.

months.focus: Master relational databases, SQL, and interact with databases using EF Core.

topics: Relational Database Concepts: Normalization, ACID properties, Transactions
SQL Deep Dive: Advanced Queries (JOINs, Subqueries, Aggregations), Stored Procedures, Indexing
Database Design Principles: ER Diagrams, Schema Design
activities: Practice SQL queries on platforms like LeetCode SQL problems or HackerRank.
Design a database schema for a new, slightly more complex application (e.g., 'E-commerce Product Catalog').
Install and configure SQL Server Express/PostgreSQL locally.

topics: Entity Framework Core: Code-First Migrations, Database-First (briefly), Data Seeding
CRUD Operations with EF Core: LINQ to Entities, Asynchronous operations
Relationships: One-to-One, One-to-Many, Many-to-Many, Eager/Lazy Loading
activities: Integrate EF Core into your existing CRUD API.
Implement all CRUD operations using EF Core, ensuring proper handling of relationships.
Write unit tests for your data access layer.

months.project_milestone: CRUD API integrated with SQL Database via Entity Framework Core, with data modeling and migrations.

months.theme: Advanced ASP.NET Core & API Best Practices
months.focus: Build robust, secure, and well-structured APIs with authentication and authorization.

topics: Authentication & Authorization: JWT Bearer Tokens, Identity Framework (basics), Custom Policies
Middleware: Custom Middleware, Order of Operations
Logging: Serilog or NLog integration, structured logging
activities: Implement JWT authentication and role-based authorization in your API.
Add global error handling middleware and logging for all requests/errors.
Explore ASP.NET Core Identity for user management (optional, if time permits).

topics: API Design Principles: RESTful API guidelines, HATEOAS (briefly), API Versioning
Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) & Mapping (AutoMapper)
Validation: Data Annotations, FluentValidation
Background Tasks & Asynchronous Processing (e.g., using Hosted Services)
activities: Refactor your API to use DTOs and AutoMapper for clean data transfer.
Implement input validation using FluentValidation.
Explore API versioning strategies (e.g., URL or Header-based).
Set up a simple background task.

months.project_milestone: Secure RESTful API with JWT authentication, authorization, robust error handling, logging, DTOs, and validation.

months.focus: Understand cloud services relevant to backend development and deploy applications.

topics: Introduction to Cloud Computing & Azure Fundamentals: Resource Groups, Azure Portal
Azure App Service: Deployment, Configuration, Scaling
Azure SQL Database: Creation, Connection, Monitoring
Azure Storage: Blob Storage (for files/images)
activities: Deploy your API to Azure App Service.
Migrate your database to Azure SQL Database.
Implement file upload/download functionality using Azure Blob Storage in your API.

topics: Docker Fundamentals: Containers, Images, Dockerfile, Docker Compose
Containerizing ASP.NET Core Applications
Introduction to CI/CD: Azure DevOps Pipelines (Build & Release basics)
Azure Key Vault for secrets management
activities: Containerize your API using Docker.
Deploy the Dockerized API to Azure App Service (container instance) or Azure Container Instances.
Set up a basic CI/CD pipeline in Azure DevOps for automatic deployment on code pushes.
Move sensitive configurations to Azure Key Vault.

months.project_milestone: API deployed to Azure, utilizing Azure SQL Database, Azure Storage, and secrets management. Basic CI/CD pipeline established. Application is containerized with Docker.

months.focus: Introduce concepts for building high-performance and scalable systems.

topics: Caching Strategies: In-memory caching, Distributed Caching (Redis/Azure Cache for Redis)
Message Queues/Brokers: Azure Service Bus / RabbitMQ (producer/consumer patterns)
Microservices Architecture: Introduction, Pros/Cons, Communication Patterns
activities: Implement caching (e.g., for frequently accessed data) using Redis in your API.
Create a simple background worker service that processes messages from a queue (e.g., email notifications).
Research and understand a simple microservice pattern and its challenges.

topics: NoSQL Databases: Introduction to Document Databases (MongoDB/Azure Cosmos DB)
Performance Tuning & Monitoring: Kestrel optimization, Database query optimization, Application Insights
System Design Fundamentals: Load balancing, Horizontal/Vertical Scaling, CAP theorem (introduction)
activities: Experiment with a NoSQL database by storing non-relational data (e.g., user profiles with flexible schemas).
Use Application Insights to monitor your deployed application's performance.
Perform basic load testing on your API and identify bottlenecks.

months.project_milestone: API enhanced with caching, integrates a message queue for async processing, and explores NoSQL database usage. Basic performance monitoring set up.

months.focus: Consolidate knowledge, prepare for interviews, and build a strong portfolio.

topics: Advanced Testing: Integration Tests (Web.API Test Host), Mocking Frameworks (Moq)
Refactoring & Code Quality: Code smells, static analysis tools
Git Advanced: Branching strategies (GitFlow, GitHub Flow), Pull Request reviews
activities: Write comprehensive integration tests for your API endpoints.
Refactor existing code for better maintainability and performance.
Practice collaborative Git workflows (e.g., by contributing to a small open-source project or with a peer).

topics: System Design Interview Prep: Common design patterns, trade-offs, whiteboard exercises
Behavioral & Technical Interview Prep: Resume review, mock interviews, common questions
Portfolio Building: Showcase projects on GitHub, write clear READMEs, personal website/blog
activities: Work through several system design case studies (e.g., 'Design Twitter', 'Design a URL Shortener').
Participate in mock interviews (coding, system design, behavioral).
Polish your GitHub portfolio, ensuring all projects have clear descriptions, setup instructions, and demonstrate key skills.
Attend relevant tech meetups or webinars.

months.project_milestone: A robust, fully tested, and well-documented portfolio project demonstrating all learned skills. Readiness for technical and system design interviews.

general_recommendations: **Daily Practice:** Stick to the 3-hour daily commitment. Consistency is key.
**Project-Based Learning:** Always aim to apply what you learn to a project. Start small, then expand.
**GitHub Profile:** Maintain an active and well-organized GitHub profile, showcasing your projects and contributions.
**Read Documentation:** Microsoft Learn and official .NET documentation are invaluable resources.
**Networking:** Engage with the C#/.NET community online (forums, Stack Overflow, LinkedIn) and locally if possible.
**Code Reviews:** Seek feedback on your code from peers or mentors to learn best practices.
**Stay Curious:** The tech landscape changes rapidly. Keep exploring new tools and concepts.

learning_platforms: Udemy/Coursera (Look for highly-rated C#/.NET Core courses)
freeCodeCamp (Good for fundamental concepts and some project ideas)
Books (e.g., 'C# in a Nutshell', 'ASP.NET Core in Action')
tools: SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) or Azure Data Studio
